# MiniOneRec

<!-- Generated by `make minionerec` (ml/eval/minionerec.py). Do not edit by hand. -->

MiniOneRec (generative retrieval: a Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model fine-tuned to emit an
item's three-token semantic ID, decoded with beam search constrained to the catalog's
SIDs), run with its published Office checkpoint on this Mac's GPU, then scored on the
same split and with the same metric code as Pop, ItemCF and SASRec in
[offline.md](offline.md). The questions: does the published result reproduce, which
users does it help, and what does a request cost.

## Setup

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Checkpoint | MiniOneRec `Office_ckpt` (Hugging Face `kkknight/MiniOneRec` @ 365a03fc): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct after SFT and GRPO, saved at RL step 1,038 of 3,456 (its trainer_state.json); bfloat16, 3.56 GB |
| Code | MiniOneRec's own `evaluate.py` (third_party/MiniOneRec @ 0cbd94de) with [a patch for Apple Silicon](../../minionerec/evaluate.py.patch): the device is `mps` when there is no CUDA, `import bitsandbytes` (CUDA-only, unused) is dropped, the model is loaded in a dtype and with an attention implementation given on the command line, and every batch is timed. Prompts, the SID prefix tree and the constrained beam search run as published. Shards: evaluate.sh's 8 (split.py's boundaries), one after another on the one GPU, joined by merge.py. Attention: transformers' eager implementation. On MPS, PyTorch's scaled_dot_product_attention returns NaN for the pad rows of a left-padded batch, and the NaN spreads to the whole sample, which then decodes no SID (see `minionerec/upstream.py`) |
| Generation | 50 beams, all returned; batch 8; length penalty 0.0; at most 256 new tokens (evaluate.sh's settings) |
| Hardware | Apple M4 Pro, 16-core GPU, 24 GB unified memory, macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit; device `mps`; PyTorch 2.6.0, transformers 4.57.1 (MiniOneRec's pinned versions); bfloat16, eager attention |
| Samples | all 4,866 test samples (2,024 users) |
| Metrics | HR@K and NDCG@K, K = 3, 5, 10, as in offline.md. **Item rule** (main): a generated SID stands for every item that has it, in the tie order (training popularity, then item_id), so the 15 pairs of items that share a SID take two ranks; **SID rule**: the rank of the target's SID among the beams, which is what MiniOneRec's calc.py computes |
| Baselines | Pop, ItemCF and SASRec exactly as in offline.md (train rows only, tuned on validation), scored on the same samples |
| Intervals | 95%, user-level bootstrap: 1,000 replicates, seed 20261106; the same replicates for every model, so paired differences are comparable and the full-split replicates are those of offline.md |

## Reproduction

MiniOneRec, arXiv:2510.24431v1, Table 1 (Office) reports MiniOneRec on this split, scored by its calc.py. The same
calc.py, unmodified, on our generations:

| Model | Metrics | HR@3 | HR@5 | HR@10 | NDCG@3 | NDCG@5 | NDCG@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper, Table 1: MiniOneRec | as reported | 0.1217 | 0.1420 | 0.1634 | 0.1088 | 0.1172 | 0.1242 |
| Our MPS generations | calc.py (its own code) | 0.1249 | 0.1402 | 0.1570 | 0.1119 | 0.1182 | 0.1237 |
| Our MPS generations | ours, SID rule | 0.1249 [0.1129, 0.1357] | 0.1402 [0.1282, 0.1518] | 0.1570 [0.1443, 0.1686] | 0.1119 [0.1013, 0.1218] | 0.1182 [0.1074, 0.1281] | 0.1237 [0.1127, 0.1335] |
| Our MPS generations | ours, item rule | 0.1247 [0.1127, 0.1355] | 0.1391 [0.1271, 0.1503] | 0.1570 [0.1443, 0.1686] | 0.1102 [0.0997, 0.1199] | 0.1161 [0.1054, 0.1259] | 0.1219 [0.1112, 0.1316] |

- **Reproduced.** calc.py on our generations differs from the paper by -0.0064 HR@10 and -0.0005 NDCG@10; the paper's HR@10 and NDCG@10 are both inside our 95% intervals.
- Constrained decoding: calc.py counted 0 generated SIDs that are not in the catalog (its CC; MiniOneRec's README asks to check that it is 0, since a non-zero count means the constraint did not hold).
- Cross-check: our SID-rule numbers equal calc.py's at every K it prints (K up to the beam width).
- Same samples, other hardware: MiniOneRec's evaluation runs bfloat16 on CUDA GPUs. Beam search keeps the 50 best partial SIDs at every step, so rounding differences can swap near-tied beams and move a target in or out of the top K.

## Which users it helps

Item rule, intervals from a user-level bootstrap inside each group (the same replicates
for every model of a group). The hypothesis was that semantic IDs, built from item text,
help most on long-tail targets and short histories; the segments test it:

- **History length**: 1-3 or 4-10 items before the target (the window is at most 10).
- **Target popularity**: head = the 20.9% of items with at least 15 training interactions (the top 20% by count, ties included; 60.5% of all training interactions); tail = the rest. 58 test targets never occur in training.
- **Target category**: level 2 of the Amazon category path (37 values, e.g. Paper, Printer Ink & Toner, Writing & Correction Supplies); cross-category = the target's category is not the category of any history item. 130 targets have no level-2 category and count as the category 'unknown'.
- **Target day**: reviewed on the same day as the last history item, or later (the split offline.md reports on).

Findings (HR@10, item rule; "significant" = the 95% interval excludes 0):

- **All samples**: MiniOneRec's HR@10 is not significantly different from SASRec's (-0.0051 [-0.0134, +0.0027]).
- **History length**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is -0.0063 [-0.0236, +0.0097] on 1-3 items and -0.0046 [-0.0141, +0.0051] on 4-10 items (1-3 items minus 4-10 items: -0.0017 [-0.0217, +0.0172]); the two groups do not differ significantly.
- **Target popularity**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is -0.0068 [-0.0201, +0.0071] on head and -0.0034 [-0.0113, +0.0046] on tail (head minus tail: -0.0034 [-0.0199, +0.0128]); the two groups do not differ significantly.
- **Target category**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is -0.0017 [-0.0106, +0.0060] on cross-category and -0.0083 [-0.0208, +0.0046] on same category (cross-category minus same category: +0.0066 [-0.0097, +0.0219]); the two groups do not differ significantly.
- **Target day**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is -0.0112 [-0.0229, +0.0008] on same day and +0.0013 [-0.0092, +0.0120] on later day (same day minus later day: -0.0125 [-0.0286, +0.0042]); the two groups do not differ significantly.

## Cost

The full run generated 4,866 samples in 5.1 h at 50 beams and batch 8: 3.76 s per sample, i.e. 63 min of this Mac's GPU per 1,000 recommendations (a test sample is one request); peak memory footprint 16.2 GiB. The 1-minute load average was at most 2.6 when a shard started (above 2: the machine was busy, so these timings are indicative). The machine swapped out 592.8 GiB while it ran, so the times include paging.

One test sample per user, 96 random users; MiniOneRec on the 16-core GPU (MPS) in bfloat16, SASRec on the CPU (Apple M4 Pro, 8 performance + 4 efficiency cores). A request at batch 1 is one user's recommendation; per-call times leave out each process's first calls (Metal kernel compilation). Memory is the process's physical footprint (Activity Monitor's figure, which includes what is allocated on the GPU), with the model weights loaded. Each configuration started when the 1-minute load average was below 2 and no Docker container ran; `docker ps` was checked every 10 s while it ran, and a configuration during which a container ran was run once more. The load column is the 1-minute load average at its start and end.

| Model | Batch | P50 per call | P90 | P99 | Users per second | Peak memory | Load, start / end |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MiniOneRec, 10 beams | 1 | 1,027 ms | 1,165 ms | 1,262 ms | 0.95 | 4.4 GiB | 1.8 / 1.1 |
| MiniOneRec, 10 beams | 8 | 5,964 ms | 5,985 ms | 5,990 ms | 1.40 | 6.1 GiB | 1.1 / 0.9 |
| MiniOneRec, 20 beams | 1 | 1,343 ms | 1,616 ms | 1,697 ms | 0.72 | 5.6 GiB | 0.9 / 1.5 |

| SASRec, PyTorch CPU, 1 thread | 1 | 0.15 ms | 0.17 ms | 0.19 ms | 6,274 | 0.2 GiB | 1.1 / 1.1 |

- `beam50_batch1_prefill` was run a second time: 5 other Docker containers ran during the first attempt.
- `beam10_batch1`: 1.4 GiB swapped out while it ran (vm_stat), so its times include paging.
- `beam50_batch1`: 506 MiB swapped out while it ran (vm_stat), so its times include paging.
- `beam50_batch8`: 7.8 GiB swapped out while it ran (vm_stat), so its times include paging.
- `beam50_batch8_once`: 945 MiB swapped out while it ran (vm_stat), so its times include paging.

- **Where the time goes.** With one new token instead of five, a 50-beam request takes 2,676 ms (P50) of its 3,110 ms: 86% is the first forward pass. Hugging Face's beam search copies the prompt (76-121 tokens) once per beam before that pass, so the model encodes the same prompt 50 times. The beams differ only in what they generate: encoding the prompt once and sharing its attention cache across the beams would remove most of that work.
- **Prompt encoded once, batch 1.** minionerec.engine encodes each prompt once and repeats its attention cache for the 50 beams (the rest of the beam search is transformers' own): 639 ms per call (P50) instead of 3,110 ms, 4.9 times faster, 1.52 users per second, peak memory 6.4 GiB, the same as per beam.
- **Prompt encoded once, batch 8.** minionerec.engine encodes each prompt once and repeats its attention cache for the 50 beams (the rest of the beam search is transformers' own): 4,315 ms per call (P50) instead of 29,104 ms, 6.7 times faster, 1.89 users per second, peak memory 14.8 GiB instead of 15.2 GiB.
- **Against SASRec.** A 50-beam MiniOneRec request is 20,091 times a single-threaded SASRec request at the median (3,110 ms vs 0.15 ms). Online, the model server runs the same SASRec encoder in ONNX Runtime and searches FAISS.

## Other settings on the same samples

Each run against the main run (test: 50 beams, batch 8, bfloat16), and two runs on the same samples whose settings differ in one value against each other (the one with the main run's value is the reference), on the samples both generated for; item rule, paired bootstrap on those samples' users. Identical top-10 = the same ten SIDs in the same order; overlap = the share of the reference's top-10 SIDs that the run also has in its top 10.

| Run | Beams / batch / dtype | Against | Samples | Identical top-10 | Top-10 overlap | HR@10, reference | HR@10, this run | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16-8-b4 | 50 / 4 / bfloat16 | test | 17 | 52.9% | 98.2% | 0.1765 [0.0000, 0.3750] | 0.1765 [0.0000, 0.3750] | +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000] |
| fp32-8-b4 | 50 / 4 / float32 | test | 17 | 0.0% | 87.6% | 0.1765 [0.0000, 0.3750] | 0.1765 [0.0000, 0.3750] | +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000] |
| once | 50 / 8 / bfloat16, prompt once | test | 4,866 | >99.9% | 100.0% | 0.1570 [0.1443, 0.1686] | 0.1570 [0.1443, 0.1686] | +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000] |
| once-trial | 50 / 8 / bfloat16, prompt once | test | 200 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 0.2300 [0.1694, 0.2917] | 0.2300 [0.1694, 0.2917] | +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000] |
| trial-200 | 50 / 8 / bfloat16 | test | 434 | 57.1% | 98.1% | 0.1359 [0.1034, 0.1695] | 0.1359 [0.1034, 0.1695] | +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000] |
| fp32-8-b4 | 50 / 4 / float32 | bf16-8-b4 | 17 | 0.0% | 88.2% | 0.1765 [0.0000, 0.3750] | 0.1765 [0.0000, 0.3750] | +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000] |

- `trial-200` has the settings of `test`; only the batches differ: a subset forms its batches from its own samples, so most batches hold other prompts with other left padding, and the kernels round differently. That alone changes 42.9% of the top-10 lists, while 98.1% of the top-10 SIDs stay; HR@10 differs by +0.0000 [+0.0000, +0.0000].

- `once` replays `test`'s batches through minionerec.engine with each prompt encoded once and its attention cache shared by the beams: **5 of 4,866 samples differ from `test`** (4,864 have the same top 10).

  Item rule on the same samples, `once` against `test`:

| Run | HR@3 | HR@5 | HR@10 | NDCG@3 | NDCG@5 | NDCG@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test` | 0.1247 | 0.1391 | 0.1570 | 0.1102 | 0.1161 | 0.1219 |
| `once` | 0.1247 | 0.1391 | 0.1570 | 0.1102 | 0.1161 | 0.1219 |

  Neither run kept its beam scores, so `minionerec.replay diff` generated the 5 batches that hold a differing sample once more both ways, with the beam scores (transformers' sequences_scores; mps, bfloat16): per beam, 26 of 26 samples gave the reference's SIDs again; with the prompt once, 26 of 26 the replay's. Over all 1,295 SIDs both paths returned for those 26 samples, the two paths move one SID's score by 0 (median), 0.0022 (P90), 0.495 (max). Per differing sample: its batch size, the first beam position where the lists part, the SID each has there, the gap between those two SIDs' scores on each path (the reference's SID minus the replay's on the per-beam path, the other way round with the prompt once), and how far the paths move that sample's shared SIDs (median / max). A near tie = both gaps measured and neither larger than that max:

| Test sample | Batch | First differing position | Reference's SID there | Replay's SID there | Gap, per beam | Gap, prompt once | Score moves | Near tie |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 624 | 8 | 19 | `<a_34><b_168><c_142>` | `<a_238><b_224><c_170>` | not among its beams | 0.343 | 0.0011 / 0.0614 | **no** |
| 2,432 | 1 | 4 | `<a_187><b_182><c_143>` | `<a_187><b_147><c_149>` | 0.139 | 0.248 | 0.148 / 0.495 | yes |
| 3,516 | 8 | 24 | `<a_250><b_174><c_0>` | `<a_11><b_137><c_43>` | 0.0596 | 0.00292 | 0.00209 / 0.0604 | yes |
| 4,425 | 8 | 26 | `<a_160><b_221><c_201>` | `<a_101><b_239><c_124>` | 0.015 | 0.0475 | 0.0022 / 0.0603 | yes |
| 4,865 | 1 | 6 | `<a_117><b_130><c_189>` | `<a_221><b_43><c_179>` | 0.0962 | 0.108 | 0.0542 / 0.252 | yes |

  So 4 of the 5 swaps are near ties, consistent with rounding; for the other 1 the cause is not known (sample 624: the replay's SID at position 19 is not among the reference's beams, so its gap on the per-beam path cannot be measured). The largest gap is 0.343.
- `once-trial` replays `test`'s batches through minionerec.engine with each prompt encoded once and its attention cache shared by the beams: all 200 samples have `test`'s 50 SIDs in the same order.
